questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- I wanted to study outside Scandinavia but stay in Europe.
- What the country could offer, such as their culture and the opportunities at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, since I was informed per email about most things.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had accommodation on campus, so I took a bus from the airport to UCD on my first day (Aircoach 700). When I arrived at UCD, I was welcomed by staff that helped me to find the reception, in which I would get my room key and student card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The first week was orientation week. I spent it to check out campus, the area, get to learn my roommates, get a bus card, go to IKEA etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a couple different types of rooms that you can choose between, and they vary in price. They differ in the number of rooms per apartment, private or sharing bathroom, bed size, cooking facilities, meal plan etc.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At UCD village we had a kitchen with oven, microwave, induction hob, toaster, kettle, large fridge, freezer etc. I know that it is possible to book accommodation in Roebuck Castle, which has lunch and dinner included in the price that you pay for your room. Additionally, you can buy all sorts of food at all times of the day on campus. A new food hall has opened, in which you can eat, drink coffee, do grocery shopping or hang out. Every Thursday there were street food trucks on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The house rent is expensive, and you will have to buy pots, pans, cutlery, mugs, toilet paper, cleaning products, bed sheets, hangers etc. if you live at UCD village since there is no equipment provided when you arrive. The one thing you get upon arrival is a new blanket and pillow.
With that said, I was happy to live on campus. My roomies became good friends, and it was an easy way to get to meet someone from the first day. Additionally, it was nice to live so close to the school. When you live on campus, you also get free gym access, and you can use their swimming pool and spa for 4 Euro. 
The campus feels like a safe place to walk around at night because there are security guards going around. When we would go to the city center, we would take bus 39A, which drives to the city in 20-30 mins for 2.30 Euro with a student leap card or took a taxi.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My studies started in January. I filled out an application for UCPH in March the year before my exchange and was offered the exchange at the end of March. After that I had to apply for admission at UCD in October with information about the modules I wanted to attend. If you are doing your bachelor thesis there, you also need to read about the different research areas they have, be clear on what you find more interesting and which supervisor you want to work with. Two weeks after the deadline I was accepted at UCD. After that you need to fill out an Online Learning Agreement, confirm your modules, and apply for the Erasmus grant (and I applied for an additional grant). The modules can be changed until a week or two after you begin the module if you don't think the module is suitable for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was offered help from my Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in the modules I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask your Erasmus coordinator for help if you are unsure about your choice of modules. There are many different options on different levels. As a pharmacy student on third year, I enjoyed taking the PHAR300xx modules.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three modules for third year students, and my bachelor thesis was for fourth year students. In Ireland their bachelor takes four years, so they write their thesis on fourth year. The Irish students usually don't have other modules on the same time as they do their bachelor thesis, so my workload was adjusted accordingly to that. I would say that my modules and my project was on an appropiate level for a third year student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I was spending more time on writing reports at UCD than at UCPH. Every report had to have an introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusion. The report was graded, and you get feedback so you can improve your writing skills. You work in pairs in the lab sessions, but you write the report alone.
Your grades over the semester from reports, presentations, groups work etc. counts % of your final grade. Thus, the final exam at UCD is different from that of UCPH, since at UCD the it doesn't count 100%. Depending on your module, the final exam may count e.g. 50% or 70% of your final grade. Additionally, all my final exams were closed book and with pen and paper.
My schedule was fixed, so I knew what time of the week I had lectures and lab sessions in my three modules. I did not have a schedule for my research project because we had to adapt to the data we obtained and my teams availability, so we planned the lab sessions once a week. The paper I wrote was shorter than it would be at UCPH. This is because you write alone as an Erasmus student, and you have electives simultaneously.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHAR30040: Advanced pharmacology of the nervous system
PHAR30030: Toxicology
PHAR30020: Endocrine, renal and reproductive pharmacology
BMOL40330: Biomolecular Science Research Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Advanced central nervous system pharmacology: If you find the brain and mental health interesting, I would recommend this course. You learn about drug addiction, the gut-brain axis, ocular pharmacology and neural developmeny.

Drug action in body systems II (Endocrine, renal and reproductive pharmacology): I liked this course because I got an in-dept understanding of all the drugs and mechanisms affecting kidneys, pancreas, adrenal glands, liver, endocrine cancers etc. You will know a lot about diabetes, hypertension, hormone cancer etc. after this course. This module has less group work than other modules but the final exam counts more.

My project was very interesting and I learned so much about neuropharmacology and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. The research team included me in their research, so it felt very meaningful to be contributing to that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy kitchen equipment and bed sheets in IKEA which was around 100 Euro. Had to throw out/donate everything when I left.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bringing or buying books wasn't necessary. You can borrow so many different books from the library for free. Most of the time we read scientific articles.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are lots of different sports clubs you can sign up for such as football, canoe, rugby, hurling, handball, tennis etc. They have several gyms and a large swimming pool and spa.
There is an international society that arranges weekend trips, so you can discover Ireland with other international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym and swimming facilities were great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Cliffs of Moher
Giants Causeway
Visit a sheep farm
Wicklow mountains / Glendalough
Belfast weekendtrip
Bray head hike
Powerscourt Gardens
The nightlife in Dublin
St. Stephens Green 
and much more

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Getting rommates helped me to meet other people as well.
Don't be afraid to talk to your Irish fellow students at school. They are very friendly and helpful.
Go on weekend trips with the International Society from UCD.
Consider living on campus despite the high costs. You will live close to so many other international students. Most of my friends also lived there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found no major cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The Irish people are friendly and have good humour.
I love their nature, particularly their beautiful coastlines and mountains.
And I like their talented live musicians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Live with roomies and close to the school
2. Apply for other grants than only Erasmus grant if needed
3. Go on lots of trips while you are there, and do it before the exam period

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Practice the topics of the modules early and try to memorize it. Most final exams are closed book.
Bring an extra credit card and a copy of your passport in case you lose it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All the things I learned. Studying at a different university gave me valuable knowledge, since I have obtained an understanding on how things can be done differently.
Additionally, I have learned about different cultures through meeting other nationalities from around the world. It was very rewarding to meet lots of new people. Some of them became good friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period. It is spread over just two weeks, so you are busy in the exam period. Additionally, the type of exam at UCD is different than at UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my exchange trip, and I have gained personal, cultural and educational experience and created good memories.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
